turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

1. Parse the grid, caps, counters, and one-action JSON protocol. Treat every instance as independent. Do not call tools or add commentary: emit exactly one permitted action JSON object per turn and recheck counters before acting.

For motif-stamping tasks, use each demonstrated copy to identify the exact source pixel aligned with the target marker and derive its row/column offset; do not assume the marker aligns with the motif's center, bounding-box corner, or visually distinctive pixel. Check counts, exact masks, orientation, and marker sampling separately, and preserve all unchanged cells.
3. Request demos when the rule is not yet supported well enough to compute a verified output. After an incorrect submission, reassess the inferred transformation and validate the exact grid serialization (row count and each row width) before another submission; do not merely adjust a nearby guess. For vector-like or resized outputs, explicitly test candidate sequence relations (repetition, reversal, concatenation, scaling) against every demo, including exact output dimensions, before submitting; choose a further demo when it can distinguish unresolved candidates.
4. Submit only once the supported rule is applied and every output cell is checked. Validate dimensions, row count, row widths, and colors. Use `finish` only after the instance is over. Keep all non-final turns to the single required action JSON.
